tagline.text: Gateway town of the Camotes, on Pacijan Island with Lake Danao and Santiago Bay

location.label: Location
location.text: Pacijan Island, Camotes Islands, Cebu Province

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: March–May dry season (June–November is the rainy season)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱3,500~5,000 (2 days, 1 night from Cebu, per person)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), then a ferry

children.text: San Francisco is a first-class municipality that covers Pacijan Island in the Camotes Islands east of Cebu, and it is the archipelago's gateway because ferries dock at Consuelo Port. With one motorbike you can see Lake Danao, Santiago Bay, caves and a rocky shoreline in a single day.
San Francisco is a town on Pacijan Island, one of the Camotes Islands in the sea east of mainland Cebu. At the 2024 census it had about
61,092 people

, making it the largest town in the islands, and its income class is first. It has 15 barangays, and the most populous is Esperanza. A causeway running through mangroves links it to Poro, the neighboring town, so the two can be treated as one island and crossed by motorbike. When you step off the boat there are many tricycle drivers calling for passengers, so agree on the destination and fare before you ride.

It is also the first place most travelers see, because Consuelo Port, where boats from Danao and Mactan dock, is in San Francisco. The name may remind you of the city in California, but here it is a quiet island town that is only 1.5 to 2.5 hours by boat from Cebu. There are no big malls or clubs. Instead you get a lake, caves, clear bays and a seaside promenade at sunset. The sights fall into three groups. The first is nature shaped by water and limestone, such as
Lake Danao
inland and
Timubo Cave
near it. The second is the sea along the southern coast, such as
Santiago Bay
and Mangodlong Rock. The third is Tulang Diot, a sandbar island to the northeast. All of them are within 15 to 30 minutes of the town center by motorbike, so it is easy to combine several in a day.

The town has an interesting history too. In 1923–25 an expedition led by Carl Guthe of the University of Michigan's anthropological museum excavated a cave on Tulang Island in this municipality and reported the remains of about 60 individuals along with grave goods. Before Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan) in November 2013, the mayor at the time had about 1,000 residents of Tulang Island evacuated, and although all roughly 500 houses on the island were destroyed, the evacuation is credited with preventing deaths. It is also a reminder that these waters lie in a typhoon path.

This is a quieter weekend destination than the resorts of mainland Cebu. However, the choice of lodging and restaurants is limited, and boat schedules change with the weather, so leave some slack in your plans. The prices and times below are approximate figures from sources checked in 2026, so confirm them locally before you go.

This calm bay on the southern coast has lodging and restaurants clustered around it, so it works as the Camotes' main visitor strip. Beach access is free, and the clear, gentle water is good for swimming with children. It is also a pleasant place for a walk along the shore at sunset.

Mangroves line both sides of the causeway between Pacijan and Poro, so even a motorbike ride across is memorable. Near the entrance to the causeway you will find the Agora market and a seaside promenade (baywalk), a good place to feel local life in the evening.

items.title: Two-day motorbike route
items.subtitle: Lake, caves and bay in one day

children.text: Arrive at Consuelo Port, leave your bags at your lodging and rent a motorbike. A day's rental is about
, with fuel extra.
Try kayaking or the zipline at Lake Danao Park and have a snack by the water.
Visit the underground pool in Timubo Cave and the Calvary viewpoint.
Head down to Santiago Bay for lunch and a swim in the sea.
Watch the sunset from Mangodlong Rock or the seaside promenade.
Cross the causeway to Poro, look around its market and coast, then go to the port in time for your boat back.
Departure ports and boat times change with the weather and the operators. The boat back runs only once or twice a day, so arrive at the port at least an hour early so you do not miss it.
It takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
by direct flight from Manila to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB).
After arriving in Cebu, go to one of the ports below and take a boat to the Camotes.
A Jomalia fast craft runs from Mactan Wharf (Lapu-Lapu City) to Consuelo Port. The trip takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
and costs about
for adults.
According to 2026 sources, the Mactan departure is around 8 AM on weekdays with a midday departure on weekends, and the return boat leaves around 10 AM. Times change often.
Check the operator's latest announcements for times and fares before boarding.
Take a bus or jeepney from Cebu City to Danao City (about
), then board a Jomalia RoRo ferry at Danao port for Consuelo, which takes about
2 hours 30 minutes
Fares differ between sources at about
, and the ferry runs four to five times a day.
A Super Shuttle Ferry runs from Pier 88 in Liloan to Poro port. The trip takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours 30 minutes
and economy class is about
From Poro port, take a motorbike or tricycle to the center of San Francisco.
Use tricycles, habal-habal (motorbike taxis) and multicabs, and if you want to see several places, renting a motorbike is the easiest option.
When renting a motorbike, ask the shop about license requirements and whether a helmet is provided.
March–May in the dry season is the most reliable time for the sea and the lake. Sources also recommend summer and the dry season.
In the rainy and typhoon season from June to November, boats are often delayed or cancelled, and some visitors report poor weather in July and August, so leave extra time if you travel then.

and may vary with local conditions.
Lodging is concentrated around Santiago Bay. Backpackers can find dorm beds or fan rooms for about
, and beach resorts start at

. There are also cheap inns near the town market, and it is wise to book ahead on holidays and in peak season. When choosing a place, also ask how far it is from the port, whether it has air conditioning and hot water, and whether it offers motorbike rental or pickup, which can cut your transport costs.

Meals center on the beachfront restaurants at Santiago Bay and the restaurants around the town market. You can eat fresh grilled seafood and local snacks, but most mid-range restaurants are inside resorts, so the choice is limited. Bring plenty of cash. If you only have one day, focus on Lake Danao, Timubo Cave and Santiago Bay and save the rest for next time.

In the evening you can enjoy local snacks and simple meals around the Agora market and the seaside promenade. Beachfront restaurants can take a long time to prepare orders, so it helps to get a table before sunset, and when you book, check whether your lodging includes breakfast.
Many visitors report that ATMs are scarce on the island, so bring plenty of cash from Cebu.
Boat times and fares change by operator and by year. Check the operator's announcements before leaving, and find out about your return ticket at the same time.
Renting a motorbike by the day is the most efficient way to get around, but roads get slippery in the rain, so take care.
Cave floors can be slippery, so wear water shoes rather than sandals and bring a waterproof bag.
On weekends and holidays, visitors from Cebu crowd in and boat tickets and lodging fill up quickly.
For rocky coasts such as Mangodlong Rock, wearing a life vest is safer because of the waves and the depth.
Save an offline map and a screenshot of the boat timetable before you leave, which makes things easier on the island.
Pack light. You will often need a tricycle or habal-habal from the port to your lodging, so a large suitcase is awkward.
In the rainy and typhoon season, boats to the Camotes can be cancelled suddenly, so do not schedule a tight connection right before your flight home.
Typhoon Yolanda in 2013 caused severe damage, including the complete destruction of homes on part of the island. Postpone your trip if a typhoon forecast is in effect.
In caves and on rocky coasts, follow the guide or staff and do not go into deep water alone.
If you are not a strong swimmer, always wear a life vest. Some places get deep suddenly.
Admission and activity fees change over time, so confirm the latest prices on site.
Because this is an island, a large hospital may not be close, so bring basic medicine and travel insurance.
